o200k: the K3 scan template TOKS_TMPL_O200K
=============================================

This file extends docs/kernels.md the way its §3 does for cl100k: §2 (atoms and classes) and the K3
contract (§1, the output paragraph of §3: ends, cap, pos, resume, lookahead to the segment end only) apply
unchanged; this file says which pieces the template makes. src/core/k3_o200k_c.c is its executable reading;
tests/model/o200k_model.py is its python transcription, diffed against hf tokenizers 0.23.2 (§5).

  toks_k3_scan_o200k_<tier>(const toks_tables *t, toks_k3_args *a)      tmpl = TOKS_TMPL_O200K


1. patterns
-----------

The template covers one family of Split patterns: behavior Isolated (or Removed with invert = true, which
gives the same pieces: the matches tile the segment, so there is never a gap to remove -- probed, §5),
leftmost-first alternation, the oniguruma semantics hf runs. Two variants exist as hub tokenizer.json files
(a third, kimi, through tiktoken: §6):

  o200k     [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]*[\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]+(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?|
            [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]+[\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]*(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?|
            \p{N}{1,3}| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n/]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+
            = CONTR_CI | DIGITS_1_3                                     (tmpl_params 0x02)
  nemo      the same without both (?i:...)? suffixes and with \p{N} for \p{N}{1,3}
            = CONTR_NONE | DIGITS_1                                     (tmpl_params 0x08)

(one line per alternative above; the real strings have no line breaks.) Sources, read from the files:
  - openai/gpt-oss-20b tokenizer.json (sha256 0614fe83cadab421296e664e1f48f4261fa8fef6e03e63bb75c20f38e37d07d3,
    the pin in tools/corpora/fetch_tokenizers.py): Sequence[Split(o200k, Isolated, invert false),
    ByteLevel(add_prefix_space false, use_regex false)], no normalizer, BPE with ignore_merges.
  - tiktoken o200k_base and o200k_harmony (tiktoken_ext/openai_public.py, tiktoken 0.7.0 -- the release that
    added o200k -- and 0.14.0; o200k_harmony reuses o200k_base's pat_str): the o200k string exactly.
  - nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16 (sha256 623c34567aebb18582765289fbe23d901c62704d6518d71866e0e58db892b5b7)
    and mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 (sha256 e11c71726323d33da7b8d6f6f269f1988931c0a52b7122bcdd8c05042974e0db),
    fetched 2026-10-03: the nemo string exactly, Isolated, then ByteLevel(use_regex false).
  - an earlier, unreviewed census run (today's census: docs/coverage.md) found 9 tokenizers with the o200k string
    (gpt-oss, Xenova/gpt-4o, Phi-4-mini, Phi-4-multimodal, Llama-4-Scout, MiniMax-M2.7, GigaChat3.1-Audio,
    Giga-Embeddings, and tiny-Cohere2 -- the last inside a two-Split Sequence, a different template) and 6 with the
    nemo string (Mistral-Nemo, Nemotron-3-Nano x2, Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, Apertus-8B, lucid-v1-nemo). Phi-4,
    Xenova/gpt-4o, MiniMax and GigaChat use Removed + invert. That run's o200k_base fallback pattern ended the
    punctuation alternative in [\r\n]* (no '/'): a transcription error; both tiktoken releases have [\r\n/]*.
  - moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (tiktoken, no tokenizer.json): o200k with a leading [\p{Han}]+, Han out of the case
    groups and no '/' -- the third parameterization, §6 (gigatoken's o200k_family has the same three knobs).

Parameters (toks_tables.tmpl_params): the template reads two cl100k fields with the same bit values,
TOKS_TP_CONTR_MASK (CONTR_NONE: no suffix; CONTR_CI: the case-insensitive suffix K below) and
TOKS_TP_DIGITS_MASK (DIGITS_1: one N atom; DIGITS_1_3: up to 3), plus §6's TOKS_TP_HAN and TOKS_TP_NO_SLASH
(layout.h). The any-class letter prefix, the [\r\n/]* tail and the \s*[\r\n]+ alternative are always there.
Any other value or bit (CONTR_CS, DIGITS_SP_RUN, DIGITS_RUN, LPREFIX_ANY, PUNCT_NL, WS_NL, anything past
0x100) is refused at load (src/core/compile.h toks_tmpl_invalid), so no table makes the kernel read a pattern
this file does not define; so are class tables whose Han bit disagrees with TOKS_TP_HAN or whose marks have
base L.

Load path: src/core/config.c's TOKS_PATTERNS maps the o200k string exactly to TOKS_TMPL_O200K with 0x02 and the
nemo string with 0x08 (toks_pattern names its template, params and class_flags; compile.c uses them), so the
gpt-oss, Mistral-Nemo and Nemotron files load; the driver's K3 call site (src/core/kernels.h toks_k3)
dispatches on t->tmpl to toks_k3_scan_o200k_<tier> (the avx2 and neon tiers, §4; the c twin on scalar).


2. classes
----------

The class tables are built with class_flags 0 (src/core/classes.h): marks keep base P and carry
TOKS_C_UPPER | TOKS_C_LOWER | TOKS_C_MARK. The pattern's five character sets are exactly class-byte tests
(each probed through hf's onig over every scalar value against the built tables, §5):

  UP   [\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]   class & TOKS_C_UPPER
  LO   [\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}]         class & TOKS_C_LOWER
  PFX  [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]                 base in {P, WS}
  P    [^\s\p{L}\p{N}]                   base = P
  N    \p{N}                             base = N;  \s = base in {WS, NL};  [\r\n] = NL

So every atom is one of: upper-only (Lu Lt: UP), lower-only (Ll: LO), both (Lm Lo, and every mark: UP and
LO), or in neither group (N, WS, NL, and P without the mark bits, including invalid atoms, which are P with no
flags, §2). An absent atom (at or past len) is in no set. No class bit beyond layout.h's is needed.


3. rules
--------

Every piece starts where the previous one ended (every atom is matched by some alternative: L atoms and
marks by O1, N by O2, the other P atoms by O3, WS and NL by O4-O6), so the pieces tile the segment. At piece
start i, with c the atom at i and c1 the next one:

Case runs. For an atom position s:
  u(s)   = the end of the maximal run of UP atoms from s (u(s) = s when the atom at s is not UP).
  K(e)   = the contraction suffix at e (CONTR_CI; empty with CONTR_NONE): the atom at e is U+0027 and
             c' in {s S t T m M d D} or c' has FOLD_S             -> the 2 atoms ' c'
             c' c'' in {r R}{e E}, {v V}{e E}, {l L}{l L}         -> the 3 atoms ' c' c''
           (c', c'' the atoms after e), otherwise empty: kernels.md §3's A1 CI test, used as a suffix.
  L1(s)  alternative 1 from s, [UP]*[LO]+K?:
           the atom at u(s) is LO -> to the end of the maximal run of LO atoms from u(s), then K;
           else some atom in [s, u(s)) is LO -> to the end of the LAST such atom, then K;
           else L1(s) does not apply.
  L2(s)  alternative 2 from s, [UP]+[LO]*K?: the atom at s is UP -> to the end of the maximal run of LO atoms
           from u(s) (possibly empty), then K; else L2(s) does not apply.

  O1 letters.
       PFX(c):      the first of L1(i+1), L1(i), L2(i+1) that applies (the piece starts at i either way:
                    c is the prefix, or c starts the run). L1(i) applies exactly when c is a mark.
       base(c) = L: L1(i), else L2(i) (one of them applies: an L atom is UP or LO).
       otherwise (N, NL): O1 does not apply.
  O2 digits.  base(c) = N -> [i, end of up to 3 consecutive N atoms)   (DIGITS_1: [i, end of c)).
  O3 punctuation. j = i if base(c) = P; j = i + 1 if c is U+0020 and base(c1) = P; otherwise O3 does not
       apply. -> [i, end of the maximal P run from j), then extended over the maximal run of atoms in
       {U+000D, U+000A, U+002F} that follows.
  O4 newline runs.  base(c) in {WS, NL}: let R = [i, k) be the maximal run of atoms with base in {WS, NL}. If R
       contains an NL atom -> [i, end of the last NL atom in R).               (kernels.md A5, WS_NL)
  O5 whitespace not before a non-space. R as in O4: k = len -> [i, k); R has >= 2 atoms -> [i, start of the
       last atom of R).                                                          (A6)
  O6 whitespace. base(c) in {WS, NL} -> [i, k) (R is one atom here).            (A7)

These rules are the regex's leftmost-first semantics written out:
  - L1: [UP]* is greedy, so it first takes [s, u(s)); [LO]+ must then start at u(s). The atom there is not UP
    (maximality), so it is LO only when it is lower-only; then [LO]+ takes the maximal LO run and K? is tried
    once (greedy, last in the alternative: the match succeeds with or without it). Otherwise [UP]* gives back
    one atom at a time from the right, and [LO]+ succeeds at the first given-back atom that is LO; its run is
    that one atom, because the atom after it is upper-only or is the non-LO atom at u(s). None -> no match.
  - L2: [UP]+ takes [s, u(s)), [LO]* the maximal LO run from u(s) (empty whenever L1(s) failed), then K?.
  - the prefix ? is greedy and alternatives are tried in order: alternative 1 with the prefix taken (L1(i+1)),
    then alternative 1 without it (L1(i)), and only then alternative 2 (L2(i+1), then L2(i)). L2(i) never
    decides: a PFX atom that is UP is a mark, which is LO too, so L1(i) applied before it.
  - O2-O6 are kernels.md's A3 (DIGITS_1_3 / DIGITS_1), A4 with the tail set {CR, LF, /}, and A5-A7.

Notes that bite (each one a case in tests/c/test_k3_o200k.c with hf's pieces, pieces shown as | ):
  - alternative 1 is exhausted, both prefix choices, before alternative 2 is tried: "\u0301A!" ->
    \u0301 | A | !   (not \u0301A | !): L1(i+1) fails (A is upper-only and ! ends the run), L1(i) applies (the
    mark is a LO atom of its own UP run) and ends after the mark.
  - L1 backtracks into an upper run: with no lower-only atom after the run, the piece ends after the run's last
    Lm / Lo / M atom: "中AB!" -> 中 | AB | !;  "A中B" -> A中 | B;  "中A's" -> 中 | A's;  "ʰA" -> ʰ | A;
    "A\u0301!" -> A\u0301 | !. A run of Lo atoms is a lower run: "中文!" -> 中文 | !.
  - an upper run then a lower run is one piece, a lower run then an upper one is two: "HTMLParser" whole,
    "ABCdEF" -> ABCd | EF, "camelCase" -> camel | Case. Lt is upper-only: "aǅ" -> a | ǅ, "Aǅb" whole.
  - the contraction is a greedy optional suffix of both letter alternatives with no word boundary: "don't",
    "DON'T", "I'M", "it'ſ" whole (U+017F folds to s, as in cl100k); "it'sx" -> it's | x; "they'r" -> they | 'r.
    A piece-initial apostrophe is only a prefix: "'llama" whole (cl100k: 'll | ama), "1's" -> 1 | 's.
    nemo has no suffix: "don't" -> don | 't.
  - a mark is PFX, UP, LO and P at once: a mark at a piece start always starts a letter piece, a P or WS atom
    before a mark is that piece's prefix ("!\u0301", " \u0301's", "\u0301\u0301" whole), but inside a
    punctuation run a mark is plain P ("!!\u0301" whole, by O3).
  - '/' is P: the P run of O3 takes every '/' before the tail, and the tail takes '/' only after a CR or LF has
    started it: "!\n/" whole, "!\n//\n/x" -> !\n//\n/ | x, "!\n/!" -> !\n/ | !. Like any P atom, '/' prefixes
    letters: "a/b" -> a | /b.
  - only U+0020 is O3's optional space; the letter prefix is any P or WS atom (tab, U+3000, an invalid byte),
    never CR, LF, L or N: "\t!" -> \t | !, " 123" ->   | 123, "\tword" whole, "\nword" -> \n | word.
  - the whitespace rules, and the lookahead stopping at the segment end, are cl100k's: "x  " -> x |   ,
    "  a" ->   |  a.

Output, cap, pos and resume are kernels.md §3's: ends strictly increasing in (pos, len], a.pos = the last end,
n <= cap; every rule classifies from its piece start forward (lookahead only), so resuming at any end written
gives the same pieces. Work is O(len): a piece consumes >= 1 atom, and an atom is visited by at most three
case-run scans (L1(i+1), L1(i), and the next piece's L1/L2).


4. for the simd tiers
---------------------

Advice, not contract (§3 is the contract). Inside a maximal run of case atoms (UP or LO) the letter rules
are a two-state walk from the piece's first case atom: the UP phase takes upper-only and both atoms and ends
at the first lower-only atom, which starts the LO phase; the LO phase takes lower-only and both atoms and ends
at the first upper-only atom -- a piece boundary, and that atom starts the next piece in the UP phase. A run
that ends while still in the UP phase splits once more, after its last both atom (L1's backtrack), or not at
all when it has none (L2). So "A中Cd" is one piece (中 is taken in the UP phase) while "Ab中Cd" is Ab中 | Cd.
The prefix attaches one atom before the run, the suffix up to three after it. gigatoken walks the same states
(CaseState, o200k_family.rs; docs/research/gigatoken-scan.md §4); for 64-byte blocks the deferral cases are
case runs, ' suffixes and CR/LF/'/' tails reaching the block end.

Speed (a review note): an o200k asm tier should transcribe this two-state walk, not the c twin. On
blocks of ascii there are no "both" atoms (Lm, Lo and marks are not ascii), so the walk reduces to cl100k's
letter run plus one more boundary: before an upper-case letter that follows a lower-case one. o200k can
therefore run at cl100k's asm speed; the c twin decodes most atoms two or three times (one L1 / L2 scan per
prefix choice), which is fine for an oracle and is not the shape to copy.

The asm parts (k3_avx2.inc / k3_neon.inc under K3_O200K; kernels.md §3.1: the c twin takes what they leave) write
the walk as masks over a 64-byte block (bit j = byte pos + j, X << 1 = "the byte before is X"):
  - case atoms: U upper-only, W lower-only, B' both (Lm, Lo, and the marks a case piece takes). A case run
    starts a piece unless the atom before it is its prefix (WS, or a P run of one atom not after U+0020);
    U & G starts one, G = ((W << 1) & ~B') | the byte after each B' run that follows a W (the LO phase meets
    an upper-only atom); an upper-only run right after B' and outside G starts one when the case run ends
    with it (L1's backtrack; a loop over those rare B'-to-U transitions).
  - marks: each P run is O3's from its first non-mark atom that no case atom follows (or its first atom
    after U+0020) to its end (Q); the marks before Q are case atoms (L1(i+1) takes them), those in Q are P.
  - O3's tail, the CR LF '/' run (CR LF under NO_SLASH) right after Q, leaves P and \s.
  - K: a ' right after a case atom (not right after a suffix) loses its start when K matches, and an
    upper- or lower-only atom right after the suffix starts a piece; a suffix the block cannot decide (a
    letter or the atom after it past the block, or a both-group atom after it) stops the decided range
    at its '.
  - digits and \s are cl100k's \p{N}{1,3} (or \p{N}) and A5-A7 terms; Han run starts (TOKS_TP_HAN).
Non-ascii atoms take their slot from a 256-entry class table; FOLD_S, a non-ascii NL, a case flag on N or WS,
one flag alone on P or none on L, and Han atoms not of base L cut the block (the twin takes the piece holding
it). CJK / hangul atoms need no lookup under TOKS_TF_CJK_B.
The neon tier (src/asm/arm64/k3_o200k_neon.S) is the same body transcribed (src/asm/arm64/k3_neon.inc).
Receipts, 2026-10-04 on tr9970x (Threadripper 9970X, cpu 18 with its sibling 2-6% busy, load 4.6-17 from other
jobs): tests/k3/fuzz_k3.c -DK3_O200K 6 x 300,000 cases (61.2M calls, every 8th through the abi checker, 30% of
the cases on mutated tables) and geo, 0 failures; test_k3_o200k with -DK3_SCAN=toks_k3_scan_o200k_avx2, 0
failures. tests/k3/bench_k3.c -DK3_O200K (30 paired rounds, 95% bootstrap interval, avx2 / c twin -O3):
o200k real64 12.06 [12.03, 12.09] (3,273 MB/s), code 13.37, wiki en / ja / ko / zh / ar / ru / hi 12.40 /
3.62 / 7.24 / 5.67 / 3.05 / 2.62 / 2.34, zh.txt 3.13, ml 5.09, eu 8.30, gpt2 tokenizer.json 7.01; nemo
real64 12.04, zh 3.12, hi 2.57; kimi real64 11.43, zh 1.64 (no CJK shortcut: Han atoms are looked up),
wiki ja 4.35; segments en L=1..256 1.53-14.76, zh L=1..256 1.46-4.18. End to end (tools/bench/e2e.c, the
gpt-oss tokenizer, en.txt in 4,096-byte chunks, 3 abba rounds, ids identical): pass 156 -> 397 MB/s (2.55x),
cold 117 -> 222 MB/s.


5. proof
--------

tests/model/o200k_model.py transcribes §2-§3 literally (classes from hf's own onig: every scalar value
through Split(Regex(set), removed) for UP, LO, PFX, P, \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{M}, \s and the eight (?i) letter
folds; the contraction group probed in 'X / 'Xe / 'Xl contexts over every scalar; §2's claims and §3's two
side claims are asserted on every scalar and every piece). tests/model/run_o200k_fuzz.py diffs it against
hf 0.23.2's Split(Regex(pattern), 'isolated') piece offsets (python binding character offsets converted to
bytes with an asserted slice check); tests/k3/o200k_run.sh diffs the c twin against the same oracle.

Receipts, 2026-10-04 UTC, hf tokenizers 0.23.2, python 3.12 under uv. One consistent run on m2ultra1 (macOS
arm64, 24 cores, load 1.32 at start, 16 jobs, seed 20261004; the model, then the c twin on the same cases):

  source (per variant)                                                     cases       o200k  nemo
  short   gen_case: class-aware strings of 0..~120 atoms                 3,000,000         0     0
  long    gen_long: 60..1000 chars (words, letters, punct, ws, digits,     300,000         0     0
          base64, paths)
  exh     every string of 0..4 atoms over REP (24 behaviours)              346,201         0     0
  small   every string of 0..6 atoms over REP_SMALL (12)                 3,257,437         0     0
  vocab   1..30 o200k vocabulary tokens (gpt-oss tokenizer.json)           300,000         0     0
  real    FLORES-200 dev + devtest (204 languages), python 3.12's        1,138,612         0     0
          stdlib, clang 21's headers (104 MB): every line, every
          paragraph, random chunks of 1..16384 chars
  model total 16,684,500 cases, 0 mismatches; hf's Removed + invert == Isolated on 3,337,202 of them.
  c twin  every source but small: 10,169,626 cases (1.60 GB, 267,307,241 pieces), 0 mismatches; each
          case also re-tiled with cap 1 and with pseudo-random caps 1..7 (resume), same ends.
  classes src/core/classes.c's tables (class_flags 0) == the onig probes on all 1,112,064 scalars
          (base class, UPPER, LOWER, MARK, FOLD_S).
  Earlier on gb10c (linux arm64, 20 cores, load 0.14 at start, 18 jobs; other seeds, the same harness
  but for the record cap): model 15,423,762 + 1,919,262 real-text cases, c twin 8,908,178 + 1,919,262,
  0 mismatches.

End to end (tests/k3/o200k_e2e.sh, m2ultra1, load 1.69 at start, 16 jobs, seed 20261004): the gpt-oss
tokenizer.json through toks_config_parse + toks_compile + toks_bpe_build (tmpl 2, params 0x02, U+0301 class
0x38), then K3 o200k with the driver's 256-piece chunks and K5, against hf's Tokenizer.encode (no special
tokens; encode_special_tokens on, all 21 added tokens being special): 2,339,213 texts (short 1,000,000, long
100,000, exh 601, vocab 100,000, real 1,138,612; 473,643,191 bytes, 180,958,949 ids), 0 mismatches.

Probe facts (identical on gb10c and m2ultra1): \p{L} 141,028 code points, LO 141,640, UP 141,271, \p{M} 2,501,
\p{N} 1,911, \s 25, [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}] 969,123, [^\s\p{L}\p{N}] 969,100; (?i:s) = {s, S, U+017F}, each other
contraction letter folds to its two ascii forms only, and the group consumes exactly those letters.

Not covered by hf: invalid utf-8 (hf takes rust strings). Its pieces follow from §2 (one P atom per byte,
no flags); tests/c/test_k3_o200k.c pins hand values for it and runs every ill-formed kind at every
position against a reference scanner. 11 small mutants of src/core/k3_o200k_c.c (no '/' in the tail, the
first instead of the last LO atom, no U+017F, L2(i+1) before L1(i), any WS as O3's space, no mark rule, 4
digits, CR/LF as a prefix, a 3-byte contraction minimum, a space after the P run, O5 not giving back) each
fail that test.


6. the kimi variant
--------------------

moonshotai/Kimi-K3 encodes with tiktoken: tokenization_kimi.py (lines 54-63) builds a tiktoken Encoding with
this pat_str (one line per alternative; the real string has no breaks):

  [\p{Han}]+|
  [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}&&[^\p{Han}]]*[\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}&&[^\p{Han}]]+(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?|
  [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{Lu}\p{Lt}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}&&[^\p{Han}]]+[\p{Ll}\p{Lm}\p{Lo}\p{M}&&[^\p{Han}]]*(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?|
  \p{N}{1,3}| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+

That is o200k with a leading Han-run alternative, Han removed from both case groups (&& is set
intersection), and no '/' in the punctuation tail. It is a parameterization of this template:

  kimi  = CONTR_CI | DIGITS_1_3 | HAN | NO_SLASH                               (tmpl_params 0x182)

In layout.h:
  TOKS_C_HAN        0x80   class bit (the last free one, reserved to TOKS_TP_HAN): \p{Han} as tiktoken's regex
                           engine resolves it. Set by classes.c only under class_flags TOKS_CLASSES_HAN, so
                           every other template's class byte keeps bit 7 clear (load refuses tables where the
                           bit and TOKS_TP_HAN disagree).
  TOKS_TP_HAN       0x80   (TOKS_TMPL_O200K) rule O0 below, and HAN atoms leave both case groups.
  TOKS_TP_NO_SLASH  0x100  (TOKS_TMPL_O200K) the O3 tail is {CR, LF}, not {CR, LF, /}.
(o200k stays 0x02 and nemo 0x08: the new bits only switch kimi's differences on.)

Rules: §3 with three changes, all keyed by the parameters:
  O0 Han (HAN), tried first. c has TOKS_C_HAN -> [i, end of the maximal run of HAN atoms), whatever the
       atoms' base classes (Lo ideographs, Lm 々 U+3005 / 〻 U+303B, Nl 〇 U+3007 and the Suzhou numerals, So
       radicals U+2E80.., Mc U+16FF0 / U+16FF1, Po U+16FE2).
  case groups (HAN): UP(x) = UPPER and not HAN, LO(x) = LOWER and not HAN, in every use: u(s), L1, L2, and
       O1's prefix tests (so a Han mark is not "a mark" for L1(i)).
  O3 tail (NO_SLASH): the maximal run of {U+000D, U+000A} (cl100k's [\r\n]*).
Everything else is §3 unchanged: the prefix set [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}], \p{N}, [^\s\p{L}\p{N}] and \s do not
mention Han, so Han atoms keep their base-class roles there -- but only after a piece has started: at a piece
start O0 wins. Derivation: [\p{Han}]+ is the first alternative and ends the match greedily (nothing follows
it), so it decides every piece that starts on a Han atom; elsewhere \p{Han} occurs only as `&&[^\p{Han}]`
inside the two case brackets, a set difference on UP and LO; the rest of the derivation is §3's.

Notes that bite (each proven against tiktoken's own engine, below):
  - O0 acts only at a piece start: "1〇" is one O2 piece (〇 is \p{N}) but "〇1" -> 〇 | 1; "!⺀" is one O3
    piece (⺀ U+2E80 is So) but "⺀!" -> ⺀ | !.
  - Han letters leave the case runs: "a中" -> a | 中, "中文a" -> 中文 | a, "A々" -> A | 々 (o200k: one piece each).
  - a P or WS atom before a Han atom is no letter prefix (the Han atom is in neither group), and a Han atom is
    never a prefix itself (O0 takes it): " 中文" ->   | 中文 (o200k: one piece).
  - a Han mark (U+16FF0) is P outside the case groups: a P-run member mid-run, an O0 atom at a piece start.
  - no '/' in the tail: "!\n/" -> !\n | /.
  - the engine is not onig: tiktoken compiles pat_str with fancy-regex, which hands character classes to the
    regex crate. Alternation is leftmost-first as in onig (the derivation above holds), but class membership
    is regex-syntax's: a bare script name is the Script property (regex-syntax 0.8.11, unicode.rs
    canonical_binary -> CanonicalClassQuery::Script; not Script_Extensions, so U+3001 、 is not Han: "a、b"
    -> a | 、b). Probed through tiktoken 0.14.0 itself over every scalar (o200k_model.py run_kimi_probes): its
    \p{Han} is exactly regex-syntax 0.8.11's Script=Han table (22 ranges, 99,030 code points, Unicode 16.0.0;
    HAN_RANGES), and its \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{M}, \s, the two case groups, [^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}] and [^\s\p{L}\p{N}]
    equal onig's on every scalar, the (?i) folds too. So kimi's class tables are the class_flags-0 tables plus
    TOKS_C_HAN on those ranges: classes.c sets the bit under TOKS_CLASSES_HAN from src/gen/han_ranges.c, which
    tools/gen/han.py generates from tiktoken's own engine (22 ranges, 99,030 code points, its sha256 checked by
    tests/c/test_k3_o200k.c); o200k_model.py reads the same file.

The proof oracle is tiktoken itself (tests/model/o200k_model.py tiktoken_pieces): an Encoding with kimi's
pat_str and a vocabulary holding every substring of every test string, so tiktoken, which looks each regex
piece up whole before merging, returns one token per piece; decoding the tokens gives tiktoken's pieces. It
is exact for any string but its vocabulary grows with the square of the length, so the kimi runs use
strings of at most 64 utf-8 bytes (KIMI_MAXB): generated (gen_kimi), exhaustive over REP_KIMI (30 behaviours,
Han atoms of every base class among them), and random slices of the real-text corpus. The piece oracle of
tools/oracle (docs/models/kimi.md) is the one for long texts.

Receipts, 2026-10-04 UTC on m2ultra1 (tiktoken 0.14.0, hf 0.23.2 for the shared probes, 16 jobs, seed 20261004;
load 1.78 before the first run, the rest of the load my own runs):
  model (run_o200k_fuzz.py --variants kimi) vs tiktoken: kshort 2,000,000, kexh 837,931 (every string of 0..4
    atoms over REP_KIMI), kreal 2,050,000 (5,000 slices from each of the 410 FLORES-200 / python / clang
    files) -- 4,887,931 cases, 0 mismatches.
  c twin (o200k_run.sh with GENARGS="--variants kimi ...", tmpl_params 0x182, the class tables plus
    TOKS_C_HAN on HAN_RANGES) vs tiktoken: the same 4,887,931 cases (173 MB, 31,359,131 pieces), 0
    mismatches, each also re-tiled with cap 1 and random caps.
  tests/c/test_k3_o200k.c runs the kimi variant everywhere (189 golden strings with tiktoken's pieces);
    4 kimi mutants of the c twin (no O0, Han kept in the case groups, '/' kept in the tail, O0 one atom
    long) each fail it.
  - tokenization_kimi.py cuts the text before the regex: every 400,000 chars, then after 25,000 consecutive
    str.isspace() or non-isspace chars (_split_whitespaces_or_nonwhitespaces; python's isspace is not \s).
    Each cut is a segment boundary -- the driver's business, not the template's (src/core/api.c walks them as
    offsets: docs/models/kimi.md §2.3, §8).
